hook.en: A coolie standing still with a heavy load on his head gets tired, yet in physics he does no work on the load. Work needs a displacement along the force.

body.en: The *scalar* product of two vectors is $\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\theta$, which is a scalar. It is commutative and distributive. For unit vectors $\hat i\cdot\hat i = 1$ and $\hat i\cdot\hat j = 0$, so $\vec A\cdot\vec B = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$.
body.kn: ಎರಡು ಸದಿಶಗಳ ಅದಿಶ ಗುಣಲಬ್ಧ A·B = AB cosθ, ಇದು ಒಂದು ಅದಿಶ. î·î = 1, î·ĵ = 0 ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ A·B = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z.

points.en: A·B = 0 means A ⟂ B (if neither is zero)

say.en: The scalar product of two vectors is vec A times vec B equals AB cos theta, which is a scalar. It is commutative and distributive. For unit vectors hat i times hat i equals 1 and hat i times hat j equals 0, so vec A times vec B equals A xB x plus A yB y plus A zB z. A B equals 0 means A ⟂ B if neither is zero.
say.kn: ಎರಡು ಸದಿಶಗಳ ಅದಿಶ ಗುಣಲಬ್ಧ A B equals AB cos theta, ಇದು ಒಂದು ಅದಿಶ. î î equals 1, î ĵ equals 0 ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ A B equals A xB x plus A yB y plus A zB z.

say.en: A A equals A squared.
cos theta equals A B / AB.

title.en: Dot product and the work done by a force

say.en: The dot product multiplies A by the part of B that lies along A, that is B cos theta.
With unit vectors, i dot i is one and i dot j is zero, so we just multiply matching components.
Work is force dot displacement. Only the part of the force along the motion does work.
Work is positive below 90 degrees, zero at 90 degrees, and negative above, as for friction.
Example: 10 newtons at 60 degrees moves a box 5 metres. The work is 25 joules.

title.en: Work done by a pull at an angle

narration.en: The box moves a distance d to the right. Only the part of the force along the displacement, F cos θ, does work: W = F·d = F d cos θ. Pull at 90° and no work is done; pull backwards (θ > 90°) and the work is negative.
narration.kn: ಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ d ದೂರ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ಥಾನಪಲ್ಲಟದ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಬಲದ ಭಾಗ F cos θ ಮಾತ್ರ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ: W = F·d = F d cos θ. 90° ನಲ್ಲಿ ಎಳೆದರೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಶೂನ್ಯ; ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ (θ > 90°) ಎಳೆದರೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಋಣ.

title.en: Work done by a constant force

body.en: The *work done* by a constant force is $W = \vec F\cdot\vec d = Fd\cos\theta$. It is positive when θ < 90°, zero when the force is perpendicular to the displacement, and negative when θ > 90°, as for friction on a sliding body. The SI unit is the joule: 1 J = 1 N m.
body.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ಬಲ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸ W = F·d = Fd cosθ. θ < 90° ಆದರೆ ಧನ, θ = 90° ಆದರೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ, θ > 90° ಆದರೆ ಋಣ (ಉದಾ. ಘರ್ಷಣೆ). ಏಕಮಾನ ಜೂಲ್: 1 J = 1 N m.

problem.en: Find the angle between the force F = (3î + 4ĵ − 5k̂) N and the displacement d = (5î + 4ĵ + 3k̂) m. Also find the work done.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the angle between the force F = (3î + 4ĵ − 5k̂) N and the displacement d = (5î + 4ĵ + 3k̂) m. Also find the work done.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the angle between the force F equals (3î plus 4ĵ minus 5k̂) N and the displacement d equals (5î plus 4ĵ plus 3k̂) m. Also find the work done.
F d equals 3 times 5 plus 4 times 4 plus minus 5 times 3 equals 15 plus 16 minus 15 equals 16 joules.
|F| = the square root of 50, |d| = the square root of 50, so cos theta equals 16 over 50 equals 0.32.
theta equals cos to the power minus 10.32 is approximately 71.3 degrees.
So the answer is W equals 16 joules; theta is approximately 71.3 degrees.

problem.en: A cyclist brakes and skids 10 m. The road exerts a friction force of 200 N opposite to the motion. Find the work done by the road on the cycle.

steps.en: The friction force and the displacement are opposite: θ = 180°.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A cyclist brakes and skids 10 m. The road exerts a friction force of 200 N opposite to the motion. Find the work done by the road on the cycle.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A cyclist brakes and skids 10 metres. The road exerts a friction force of 200 newtons opposite to the motion. Find the work done by the road on the cycle.
The friction force and the displacement are opposite: theta equals 180 degrees.
W equals 200 times 10 times cos 180 degrees equals minus 2000 joules.
So the answer is minus 2000 joules.

body.en: If a force is always perpendicular to the motion, it does no work however large it is: the tension on a stone whirled in a circle, or the normal reaction on a block sliding on a level floor.
